did_you_know.text: Did you know? Amaziah became king of Judah at the age of twenty-five and reigned in Jerusalem for twenty-nine years. His mother was named Jehoaddan and was from Jerusalem.
Did you know? Amaziah punished his father’s murderers but did not kill their sons. In doing so, he followed the principle stated in the Torah: “Each person shall die for his own sin.”

Did you know? Amaziah organized Judah’s army by ancestral families, with commanders of thousands and commanders of hundreds, and found that there were three hundred thousand fighting men aged twenty and older.
Did you know? Amaziah hired one hundred thousand fighting men from Israel for one hundred talents of silver, but later he was told to send them back and not take them to war.
Did you know? When Amaziah was concerned about losing the money he had paid the army of Israel, the man of God replied, “The LORD can give you much more than that.”
Did you know? Amaziah led his army to the Valley of Salt and struck down ten thousand men of Seir, that is, the Edomites.
Did you know? After his victory over Edom, Amaziah brought the gods of the people of Seir to Jerusalem, set them up as gods, bowed down to them, and burned incense to them.

Did you know? Amaziah invited Joash, king of Israel, to face him in battle, and Joash replied with a parable about a thistle in Lebanon that was trampled by a wild animal after daring to compete with a cedar.
Did you know? After Judah’s defeat at Beth-shemesh, Joash broke down a section of Jerusalem’s wall four hundred cubits long, from the Gate of Ephraim to the Corner Gate.

Did you know? After Amaziah turned away from following the LORD, conspirators plotted against him in Jerusalem. He fled to Lachish, but the conspirators killed him there. They then carried him back and buried him with his ancestors in Jerusalem.
